flash.title: Install and back up
flash.lead: Put OpenDigitalRadio on your radio, back it up, or put it back. Works over USB in Chrome or Edge on a computer.
flash.start.title: What do you want to do?
flash.task.install.text: Put OpenDigitalRadio on your radio, or update it.
flash.task.backup.text: Save your channels, settings and calibration to a file.
flash.task.restore.text: Put a radio back from a backup file made here.
flash.log.summary: This page reports which radio and firmware you install, restore or back up, and whether it worked, so we can find failures.
flash.log.sent: Sent: a random ID, the task, the radio model, the firmware version and features, and the result or error. Never your firmware files, backups or radio data.
flash.log.kept: Stored with your IP address. Custom build requests are stored the same way even with reporting off, to stop abuse. Never sold or shared.
flash.log.choices: Opt out with ?reporting=0, or --no-reporting in odrflash.
flash.log.contact: To see or delete your data, email
flash.start.privacy: Firmware comes from this site. Your stock firmware file, backups and radio data stay on your computer.
flash.support.none: This browser can't talk to radios. Use Chrome or Edge on a computer.
flash.support.usb: This browser can't install firmware. Use Chrome or Edge on a computer.
flash.support.serial: This browser can't talk to a radio running OpenDigitalRadio. Use Chrome or Edge on a computer.
flash.sim.banner: Practice mode: the radio is simulated.
flash.sim.image: Practice mode uses a made-up firmware.
flash.sim.enter_bootloader: Practice: put the radio in update mode
flash.radio.title: Which radio do you have?
flash.radio.detect_hint: Already running OpenDigitalRadio? Plug it in, switch it on and let the page find it.
flash.build.title: Which features?
flash.build.lead: Full has everything this radio can run. Turn single features on or off below to get a custom build.
flash.build.unavailable: {error} You can also build it yourself (below).
flash.build.on_request: The firmware is prepared for you when you continue, usually in under a minute.
flash.build.no_image: No firmware yet. Go back one step.
flash.build.self_text: Build it with this command, then choose the file here.
flash.now.title: What's on the radio now?
flash.now.odr_text: Plug the radio in and switch it on. The page checks it.
flash.now.stock_text: What it came with from the factory.
flash.now.unknown_text: You'll need the stock firmware file.
flash.now.reading_codec: Saving the voice codec from the radio…
flash.now.which_version: Original firmware version, if you know it:
flash.now.stock_backup_later: The original firmware can't be backed up yet. Right after the install, the page saves your channels, settings and calibration, which the install doesn't touch.
flash.now.stock_backup_planned: Right after the install, the page saves your channels, settings and calibration, which the install doesn't touch.
flash.backup.lead: Saved as a file on your computer.
flash.backup.after_lead: The radio still holds your original channels and calibration. Save them now.
flash.backup.saved: Backup saved ({size} KB). Keep it somewhere safe.
flash.backup.incomplete: Some parts couldn't be read: {files}. The rest is saved.
flash.backup.note_after: Saved right after OpenDigitalRadio was installed over the original firmware, before anything else changed.
flash.backup.task_lead: Plug the radio in and switch it on with OpenDigitalRadio running.
flash.backup.add_stock: Also put my stock firmware file in the backup (so restore can put the original firmware back)
flash.backup.stock_none: A radio with its original firmware can't be backed up here yet. Choose Install: the page saves a backup right after.
flash.codec.title: Voice codec
flash.codec.lead: DMR voice needs the radio maker's voice codec. It isn't part of OpenDigitalRadio, so it either stays in the radio or comes from your stock firmware file.
flash.codec.mode.keep: Keep the codec that's in the radio
flash.codec.mode.merge: Take the codec from my stock firmware file
flash.codec.key_from_radio: The radio's update key was read from the radio.
flash.codec.stock_unknown: not a stock firmware file this page knows
flash.write.title: Install
flash.write.bootloader_title: Put the radio in update mode
flash.win.title: On Windows: install the update-mode driver (once per computer)
flash.win.failed: On Windows this usually means the update-mode driver isn't installed yet. Install it, then try again:
flash.win.step1: Download Zadig and run it (it needs no install):
flash.win.step2: Put the radio in update mode (above) and plug it in.
flash.win.step3: In Zadig's list pick “{product}”. The USB ID boxes show {usb_id}. If it isn't listed, choose Options › List All Devices.
flash.win.step4: Choose WinUSB as the driver (right of the green arrow) and click Install Driver, or Replace Driver. Wait until Zadig says it succeeded.
flash.win.step5: Unplug the radio, put it back in update mode and try again.
flash.win.note: Only update mode needs this driver. Other tools that use the same USB device (the maker's upgrade tool, the MD-380's CPS) need their own driver back: in Device Manager, uninstall the device with “Delete the driver software”, then plug it in again.
flash.write.unexpected: The radio calls itself “{what}”, which doesn't match this model. Check you picked the right radio.
flash.write.failed: The install stopped: {error}. Nothing is lost: put the radio in update mode and install again.
flash.f4.codec_text: The update goes over the cable. The voice codec stays in the radio, so there's no stock file to find and no update mode.
flash.f4.title: Install
flash.f4.lead: Keep the radio on and plugged in until the page says it's done. Its screen freezes while it installs; that's normal.
flash.f4.safety: If it stops halfway, nothing is lost. The radio starts in update mode the next time you switch it on, and you can finish there.
flash.f4.enter_failed: The radio didn't start the install: {error}. Nothing was changed. Use update mode below instead.
flash.f4.after_fail: If the radio doesn't answer any more, switch it off and on. It starts in update mode, and you can finish below.
flash.f4.repick: The radio reconnected under a new name. Pick it once more to go on.
flash.f4.kept: Part of the codec shares space with the firmware. A copy was saved as {file} first, and the codec is put back unchanged.
flash.f4.ok: Done and checked. The radio restarts now.
flash.f4.same: The radio already had this firmware. The radio restarts now.
flash.done.title: Check the radio
flash.done.lead: The radio restarts. When its screen is back, check that everything works.
flash.done.ready: All good: OpenDigitalRadio runs and DMR voice works.
flash.done.no_codec: The radio has no voice codec: FM works, DMR voice doesn't. Go back to the codec step and take it from your stock firmware file.
flash.restore.title: Choose your backup file
flash.restore.lead: A backup bundle (.zip) saved by this flasher.
flash.restore.to_odr_text: The firmware and codec as they were, then the codeplug.
flash.restore.to_stock_text: The manufacturer's firmware from your stock file, codec included.
flash.restore.stock_needed: Choose the stock firmware file: it holds the firmware to write back and the bootloader key.
flash.restore.done_stock: The radio restarts on its stock firmware.
flash.restore.spi_note: The memory chip (codeplug, calibration) wasn't changed. To put your stock codeplug back, write it with the manufacturer's programming software.
flash.restore.codeplug_lead: When the radio has restarted, connect it: the flasher compares its codeplug with the backup and writes back what differs.
flash.restore.codeplug_refused: {n} of {total} sectors were refused by the radio (areas it protects).
flash.err.load: The page didn't load completely. Reload it.
flash.err.security: The browser blocked USB. Open this page over https.
flash.err.no_serial: This browser can't talk to the radio. Use Chrome or Edge.
flash.err.no_usb: This browser can't install firmware. Use Chrome or Edge.
flash.err.no_answer: The radio didn't answer. Is it switched on and running OpenDigitalRadio? Close any other program that uses the radio.
flash.err.unknown_board: This page doesn't know the radio “{board}”.
flash.err.wrong_board: The radio says it is a {board}, not a {name}.
flash.err.not_in_bootloader: The radio isn't in update mode.
flash.err.need_stock_for_key: Choose your stock firmware file first: the page needs it to unlock update mode.
flash.err.stock_as_image: That's a stock firmware file, not an OpenDigitalRadio image.
flash.net.found: The radio is set to USB network mode, so the page can't talk to it.
flash.net.none: No radio found. Check the cable, and that the radio is on and running OpenDigitalRadio.
flash.net.step1: On the radio: Tools > USB network (OK, 5, 4), choose “Switch USB to serial”.
flash.net.step2: If Settings > Connections > USB network at start is on, turn it off, or the radio starts as a network adapter again.
home.codec: The AMBE voice codec isn't included. The installer keeps the one in your radio or takes it from your stock firmware file.
home.f_voice_text: DMR Tier II and FM. CTCSS/DCS, VOX, scan, dual watch, VFO.
home.f_data_text: Text messages, location (LRRP, ARS), emergency, call alert, radio check.
home.f_network_text: MMDVM hotspot, single frequency repeater, APRS. Over USB: status page, rigctld, SNMP, TFTP.
radio.note.dm1701: FM, DMR voice and data, text messages, the hotspot and the USB network services work on air.
radio.note.dm32: Not yet tested on a radio.
radio.note.md380: Not yet tested on a radio. No CTCSS/DCS yet.
radio.note.dm1801pro: Early bring-up. It boots on a radio; display, keys and storage work. FM and DMR are not yet checked on air, and DMR has no voice yet.
radio.note.db25d: Early work: FM receive only, no transmit or DMR yet. Not yet tested on a radio.
planned.note.tyt-md-uv380--md-uv390-rete: Same hardware family as the DM-1701. Next in line.
planned.note.tyt-md-9600-retevis-rt90: Mobile radio, same hardware family as the DM-1701.
planned.note.radioddity-gd-77-tyt-md-760: Needs a radio for development. A DM-1801 bought new today is not v1.
flash.backup.opt.all_text: Firmware, codec, calibration, codeplug and the rest of the memory chip, including the stock firmware's resources.
flash.backup.opt.firmware_text: The firmware memory (firmware and codec) and the factory calibration.
flash.backup.opt.codeplug_text: Channels, contacts, zones and settings, and the factory calibration.
flash.codec.need_key: The page needs it to unlock update mode.
flash.codec.need_codec: The codec comes from your stock firmware file.
flash.codec.key_saved: This browser remembers the radio's update key.
flash.codec.codec_from_radio: The codec was saved from the radio and checked. This browser keeps a copy, so an install that stops halfway can still be finished.
flash.codec.codec_from_radio_unsaved: The codec was saved from the radio and checked. This browser can't keep a copy (private window?), so if the install stops halfway you'll need the stock firmware file.
flash.codec.codec_saved: The codec this browser saved from your radio earlier is put back.
flash.codec.or_connect: If the radio already runs OpenDigitalRadio, go back and pick that instead: then the page checks the codec in the radio.
flash.codec.anyway_text: To take the codec from your stock file anyway, choose the file, then pick “Take the codec from my stock firmware file” below.
flash.restore.to_codeplug_text: Channels, contacts and settings as backed up. The firmware stays as it is.
flash.build.untested: OpenDigitalRadio hasn't run on a {name} yet. This is for testers: save a backup first and keep your stock firmware file.
flash.build.wrong_options: The firmware came back without {name}={value}. Try again.
flash.err.wrong_option: The radio says it is an {board}, so its {option} is {value}. Go back to the build step and pick that.
flash.sim.try_c7000: Practice with a DM-1801 Pro (original firmware)
radio.c7_step1: Connect the programming cable to the radio and to the computer.
radio.c7_step2: Open the flasher and choose the cable. A radio that runs ODR is found as it is: no keys, no switching off.
radio.c7_step3: Otherwise switch the radio off, and on again when the page asks. You don't hold any keys. The screen stays dark and the LED on top blinks yellow while the radio is in loader mode.
flash.c7.radio_unconfirmed: not confirmed (the bootloader has no known ID)
flash.c7.retry_safe: Nothing is lost. The radio's bootloader and the loader in its chip are never written, so the radio can always be connected again, whatever is in its memory now.
flash.c7.retry_how: Try again. If the page can't reach the radio any more, switch the radio off, press Back to connect it again, and switch it on when asked. An install that stopped halfway continues where it stopped: only what still differs is written.
flash.c7.bundle_note: program-memory.bin is the radio's whole 1 MB program memory as read through the loader, from 0x03000000. data-memory.bin is the 16 MB data memory: channels, contacts, settings and the factory calibration.
flash.c7.visual.cable: The radio can be on or off for now.
flash.c7.visual.cycle: Switch the radio off, then on again with the power knob.
flash.c7.visual.led_wait: LED: slow yellow blink. The radio is in loader mode and waiting.
flash.c7.visual.led_busy: LED: fast yellow blink. Data is moving: don't touch the radio or the cable.
flash.c7.visual.screen_off: Screen: dark. This is expected in loader mode.
flash.c7.visual.screen_loader: Screen: "PC Loader Connected". The keys do nothing until the radio restarts.
flash.c7.visual.screen_on: Screen: on, the radio runs normally.
flash.c7.connect.title: Connect your {name}
flash.c7.connect.step_cable: Plug the programming cable into the radio's accessory jack (the speaker-mic socket) and into this computer. Use a charged battery.
flash.c7.connect.step_choose: Press "Choose the cable" and pick the cable's port in the list the browser shows.
flash.c7.connect.no_cable: The cable isn't in the list?
flash.c7.connect.which_port_text: Unplug the cable and plug it in again while the list is open: the entry that disappears and comes back is the cable. It is often named after its chip (FTDI, CH340, CP210x, PL2303), "usbserial" on a Mac or "COM" with a number on Windows.
flash.c7.connect.looking: Looking for the radio on the cable…
flash.c7.connect.odr_loading: Starting the loader from ODR. No keys and no switching off: the radio's screen shows "PC Loader Connected" in a moment.
flash.c7.connect.odr_failed: ODR did not hand over to the loader ({error}). Use the switch off and on method instead.
flash.c7.connect.odr_restart: This ODR build can't hand over to the loader by itself, so the page restarts the radio to meet its boot ROM. This takes a few seconds.
flash.c7.connect.odr_restart_failed: The restart didn't reach the loader. Switch the radio off and on instead:
flash.c7.connect.step_on: Switch it on again. The page is listening and takes over within a second.
flash.c7.connect.no_keys: Don't hold any keys. The screen stays dark and the LED on top starts to blink yellow slowly: that is loader mode, and it is expected.
flash.c7.connect.hint_order: Switch it off and on once more. The page has to be listening first; it is listening now.
flash.c7.connect.hint_plug: Push the cable plug fully into the radio. A loose plug is the most common cause.
flash.c7.connect.hint_battery: Use a charged battery: a radio that starts on a weak battery may not reach the loader.
flash.c7.connect.hint_ch340: Your cable has a CH340 chip. Some CH340 cables are reported not to reach the chip's boot loader. If the radio is still not found, try a cable with an FTDI chip.
flash.c7.connect.no_rom: The radio didn't answer within three minutes.
flash.c7.connect.rom_found: The radio answered. Starting the loader…
flash.c7.connect.load_failed: Starting the loader failed ({error}). Switch the radio off and try again.
flash.c7.connect.found_stub: The loader is still running from before.
flash.c7.connect.found_odr_stub: The loader is running. ODR handed over.
flash.c7.connect.checking: Checking the memory chips and which radio this is…
flash.c7.connect.led_rom: Look at the radio: the LED on top blinks yellow slowly and the screen is dark. Continuing…
flash.c7.connect.led_odr: Look at the radio: the screen shows "PC Loader Connected" and the LED on top blinks yellow slowly. Continuing…
flash.c7.connect.wrong_radio: This firmware is for the {name}, but the radio on the cable is a {other}. Nothing was written. Start over and choose the {other}.
flash.c7.check.title: Back up and check the radio
flash.c7.check.lead_first: Before anything is written, the page reads the radio's program memory: it is your way back to the stock firmware, and the source of the radio's codec, which ODR carries over. The backup is saved as a download and kept in this browser.
flash.c7.check.lead_update: The radio runs ODR. An update only needs the codec slot checked, a few seconds. You can back up more if you like.
flash.c7.check.opt_progmem_first: Required before the first install: the stock firmware and its codec.
flash.c7.check.opt_q128_text: Channels, contacts, settings and the factory calibration. Never written by this page; worth a copy anyway.
flash.c7.check.is_unknown: a firmware this page doesn't recognize; it is in your backup
flash.c7.check.saved_both: saved as a download and kept in this browser
flash.c7.check.saved_download: saved as a download (this browser can't keep a copy: private window?)
flash.c7.check.saved_slot: the codec is kept in this browser
flash.c7.codec.keep: ODR's codec slot in the radio checks out and stays as it is.
flash.c7.codec.from_radio: The codec from the radio's stock firmware (version {tag}) is copied into ODR's codec slot.
flash.c7.codec.from_browser: The codec this browser kept from this radio is written into the codec slot.
flash.c7.codec.from_file: The codec from your file {name} is written into the codec slot.
flash.c7.codec.none: No codec: FM works, DMR voice stays off.
flash.c7.codec.action: DMR voice needs the radio's own codec
flash.c7.codec.action_text: The page found no codec it knows in the radio. Choose a program memory backup of this radio (program-memory.bin from an earlier backup) or a stock firmware file the page knows.
flash.c7.codec.pick: Choose a backup or stock file
flash.c7.codec.without: Install without the codec (FM only; add the codec later)
flash.c7.codec.none_risk: DMR voice stays off until you install again with a codec source.
flash.c7.write.title: Install
flash.c7.write.careful: Leave the radio and the cable alone until the page says it is finished.
flash.c7.write.careful_text: The LED blinks fast while data moves. Only the 4 KB blocks that differ are written, and each one is read back and checked. If anything stops it, nothing is lost: run it again.
flash.c7.write.ok: Done: {written} blocks written, {same} already right, every block verified. The radio restarts now.
flash.c7.write.lost: the loader doesn't answer any more
flash.c7.write.map_label: The radio's program memory, one square per 4 KB block
flash.c7.write.map_slot: blue line: the codec slot from {addr}
flash.c7.done.lead: The page asks ODR on the radio what it runs, over the same cable.
flash.c7.done.ready: ODR runs with its codec: FM and DMR voice are ready.
flash.c7.done.no_codec: ODR runs, but without a codec: DMR voice is off. Install again with a codec source.
flash.c7.done.no_answer: The radio didn't answer yet. If its screen shows ODR, it worked: this build may have the debug link off. Otherwise switch it off and on, and check again.
flash.c7.done.backup_kept: Keep the backup you downloaded: it puts the stock firmware back (Restore, on the start page).
flash.c7.done.next_time: Next time, updating needs no switching off: ODR hands over to the loader by itself.
flash.c7.done.next_time_power: This build doesn't include the loader hand-over (CONFIG_STUB_ENTRY). The next update tries to restart the radio into loader mode by itself, and asks you to switch it off and on only if that doesn't work.
flash.c7.backup.lead: The loader reads both memories whatever firmware the radio runs. Every block is checked against the radio's own checksum.
flash.c7.backup.progmem_text: 1 MB: the firmware and the codec.
flash.c7.backup.q128_text: 16 MB: channels, contacts, settings, the factory calibration.
flash.c7.restore.title: Put the program memory back
flash.c7.restore.lead: Writes the backup's firmware and codec slot back exactly, from 0x0300C000 up. The bootloader isn't written. Only the blocks that differ are written.
flash.c7.restore.done: Done: {written} blocks written, {same} already right, every block verified. The radio restarts into the restored firmware.
flash.c7.restore.other_radio: This backup is from another radio model.
flash.c7.restore.data_note: The data memory in the backup is not written back by the page: the radio's own copy is used.
